prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: EN · Issue tracker (language en).
Grid: 6 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "ID" · longest unbreakable word 39px · one-line width 75px
  col 2: header "Title" · longest unbreakable word 92px · one-line width 394px
  col 3: header "Severity" · longest unbreakable word 59px · one-line width 59px
  col 4: header "Assignee" · longest unbreakable word 66px · one-line width 66px
  col 5: header "Status" · longest unbreakable word 61px · one-line width 77px
  col 6: header "Updated" · longest unbreakable word 62px · one-line width 87px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
This table cannot fit without splitting words at 360px. You MAY choose a total wider than 359px (the reader then scrolls horizontally), or squeeze and accept splits — a design decision.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"A phone-width issue tracker for scanning and triaging bugs: identify the issue, judge urgency/status, see ownership and recency.","reading":"Readers scan top-down by row: ID and title locate the issue, then severity/status/assignee/updated answer triage questions. Cross-row comparison is mainly severity, status and recency.","groups":["ID + Title: together form the row identity and the primary scan path","Severity + Status: both express triage state and are compared across rows","Assignee + Updated: secondary ownership and recency metadata, read after triage state"],"keep_intact":["ID strings such as BUG-2041, including the hyphen","Severity and status values and their headers","Assignee names","Updated dates or relative times"],"may_wrap":["Title at word boundaries","Headers when space is tight","Two-word status or updated values at spaces, not inside words","Assignee names at spaces"]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r1A: widths [96, 140, 80, 87, 98, 108] · table 610×580px · row heights [36, 83, 83, 129, 83, 60, 106] · column headers wrapped 0/6 · tallest cell 5 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 250px
Design r1B: widths [96, 119, 80, 87, 98, 108] · table 589×673px · row heights [36, 106, 83, 129, 106, 83, 129] · column headers wrapped 0/6 · tallest cell 5 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 229px
Design r1C: widths [96, 160, 80, 87, 98, 108] · table 630×487px · row heights [36, 83, 60, 83, 83, 60, 83] · column headers wrapped 0/6 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 270px

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}

log.raw: {"critique":[{"design":"r1A","good":"Even, legible column rhythm; headers stay on one line; no mid-word splits; Title at 140px keeps rows from becoming extreme (only one 5-line row).","problems":"The table is 610px wide inside a 360px box — the reader must scroll past Assignee, Status and Updated to answer any triage question, and ID+Title alone (236px) barely fit, so the primary scan path is cramped while the columns that cause the overflow (Status 98, Updated 108) are the ones nobody needs first. Rows are also uneven (36/83/83/129/83/60/106) so the eye loses the row band.","cause":"Roughly 77px of pure slack in the fixed columns: ID 96 where 60 suffices (BUG-2041 is 39px), Status 98 where 82 suffices, Updated 108 where 83 suffices.
